mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS MA(3) > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) above 135,000 suggests growing hiring momentum, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investor confidence improves.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite PAYEMS > 135,000 for at least 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of more than 2% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak demand curtails corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or neutral when HOUST declines by >2% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production index) falls below 109 for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to supply-side weakness and reduced corporate optimism.
regime_hint: supply shock or soft landing risk
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified INDPRO regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return as lower labor market friction supports equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) when UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2020 averages predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as strong demand supports earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2020_avg and RSAFS > 2020_avg for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive despite both proxies above 2020 averages for the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 for three consecutive months in a regime of falling CPIAUCSL (inflation), S&P 60-day forward returns are expected to be positive due to strong labor market offsetting inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150,000 for 3 months and CPIAUCSL < previous month for 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the defined labor and inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP) by 3% or more over a 3-month window predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as supply contraction erodes corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly < previous month - 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified contraction regime.
